subject: English
topic: Cloze Test III — Passage with Blanks (W11 B2)

questions.stem:
Read the passage and fill in blanks Q1–Q5:

The importance of physical exercise cannot be (1)___. Regular exercise not only keeps the body fit but also (2)___ the mind. Studies have shown that people who exercise regularly are less (3)___ to stress and depression. Exercise (4)___ the release of endorphins, chemicals in the brain that act as natural painkillers and mood (5)___ . Even a thirty-minute walk each day can make a significant difference to one's overall health.

Choose the best word for blank (1):
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'The importance cannot be overstated' = it is so important it is impossible to emphasise it too much. OVERSTATED is the precise word in this fixed collocation. Trap: UNDERSTATED = used when something is described as LESS important than it is (opposite error — 'cannot be understated' is grammatically odd and logically confused); EXAGGERATED = not the standard word in this fixed phrase.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q1]

Choose the best word for blank (2) — 'Regular exercise not only keeps the body fit but also (2)___ the mind.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. The sentence uses 'not only...but also' to show two positive benefits of exercise: keeping the body fit AND something positive for the mind. SHARPENS = makes the mind keener and more alert. Context: the whole passage argues for the benefits of exercise, so the missing word must be positive. Trap: Weakens and Confuses = negative (contradict the pro-exercise theme); Restricts = negative and unrelated to mental function.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q1]

Choose the best word for blank (3) — 'people who exercise regularly are less (3)___ to stress and depression.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Less prone to stress' = less likely to experience or be affected by stress. 'Prone to' = liable to suffer from (negative tendency). This is the fixed collocation: prone to + illness/problem. 'Less prone' = reduced vulnerability. Trap: Immune to = completely protected from (too strong — 'less immune' is not idiomatic); Resistant to = able to withstand ('less resistant' would mean more vulnerable — opposite meaning); Accustomed to = used to/familiar with (not the right word for health vulnerability).

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q1]

Choose the best word for blank (4) — 'Exercise (4)___ the release of endorphins...'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Exercise triggers the release of endorphins' = exercise causes/initiates the release. TRIGGERS = causes something (especially a reaction or process) to begin. The passage states endorphins are beneficial (painkillers, mood elevators), and exercise initiates this process. Trap: Suppresses = stops or reduces (opposite — would mean exercise reduces endorphins); Prevents = stops entirely (would mean exercise stops endorphin release); Delays = postpones (wrong direction).

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q1]

Choose the best word for blank (5) — '...chemicals in the brain that act as natural painkillers and mood (5)___.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Mood elevators' = substances or activities that raise/improve one's mood. The context: endorphins are described positively as 'natural painkillers AND mood ___', implying another positive effect = mood elevation. 'Mood elevators' is the standard medical/psychological collocation. Trap: Depressants = lower mood (opposite, e.g., alcohol is a depressant); Suppressors = suppress/lower (negative); Enhancers is close in meaning but 'mood elevators' is the more established term for endorphins.

questions.stem:
Read the second passage and fill in blanks Q6–Q10:

India's space programme has come a long (6)___ since its humble (7)___ in the 1960s. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has (8)___ global attention by successfully launching satellites and spacecraft at a (9)___ fraction of the cost of other space agencies. ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission proved that India could (10)___ deep space exploration without breaking the bank.

Choose the best word for blank (6):
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Come a long way' is a fixed English idiom meaning 'to have progressed greatly from a humble beginning'. Only WAY completes this standard expression. Trap: Path, Distance, Road — while they have similar denotative meanings, the idiomatic collocation is specifically 'come a long WAY'. None of the others form this fixed phrase.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q6]

Choose the best word for blank (7) — '...since its humble (7)___ in the 1960s.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Humble beginnings' = the standard collocation for a modest or small start. 'Since its humble beginnings in the 1960s' = from the time when it started in a small way. BEGINNINGS collocates with 'humble' far more naturally than other options. Trap: Origins = has similar meaning but 'humble origins' is more common for a person than an organisation's history; Attempts = implies repeated trying (not the same as starting); Failures = negative (contradicts the positive narrative).

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q6]

Choose the best word for blank (8) — 'ISRO has (8)___ global attention...'
questions.explanation: C is correct. GARNERED = gathered or accumulated (especially praise, attention, or support). 'Garnered global attention' = earned and collected worldwide recognition. This is the most precise and formal option for this context. ATTRACTED = also correct and commonly used ('attracted attention'), but GARNERED is stronger and more specific to achievements. In SSC fill-in-blank questions, the most precise match wins. Trap: Diverted = turned away (negative — means redirecting attention elsewhere); Deflected = turned aside (opposite of attracting).

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q6]

Choose the best word for blank (9) — '...at a (9)___ fraction of the cost of other space agencies.'
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'At a mere fraction of the cost' = at only a very small portion of the cost. MERE emphasises the smallness or insignificance of the fraction — it is the precise word for expressing that ISRO's costs are surprisingly low. 'A mere fraction' is a fixed expression used to highlight cost efficiency. Trap: Large and Substantial = imply the cost is high (opposite of ISRO's reputation for low-cost launches); Tiny = also possible but 'a tiny fraction' is less idiomatic than 'a mere fraction' in formal prose.

questions.stem:
[Refer to the same passage from Q6]

Choose the best word for blank (10) — 'ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission proved that India could (10)___ deep space exploration without breaking the bank.'
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Conduct deep space exploration' = carry out or undertake space exploration. The sentence proves India's CAPABILITY to DO deep space missions affordably. CONDUCT = to carry out or perform (a scientific mission, survey, or operation). 'Conduct an exploration/mission' is the standard collocation. Trap: Avoid and Prevent = mean not doing it (opposite of what the sentence says — the Mars Mission proved India CAN do it); Delay = postpone (unrelated to proving capability).
